I have not read any books in this genre before. I have a limited politics background and do not want to be turned off right away but choosing the wrong book. Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Not a primary genre of mine but I recently became interested in this book:

The Imperial Presidency by Jr. Arthur M. Schlesinger

The Imperial Presidency traces the growth of presidential power over two centuries, from George Washington to George W. Bush, examining how it has both served and harmed the Constitution...

Awesome! There are some real eye openers in there about how we've gotten to this point. The trend from wars being officially declared, as intended, to presidentially directed "peacing keeping operations" and such. The parts about foreign affairs and international agreements are also interesting when put into our current TPP perspective. Just keep in mind it's a history book and it can be pretty dry.

This is partly why I became interested. With all the big political controversies recently and the campaign for President starting I want to expand my perspective I guess. I'm very interested on how reading a few books like this will affect my views on current events. I appreciate the recommendation.

Ah, if that is your objective then perhaps you might find War is a Racket interesting as well. I haven't read it yet but it is on "the list" as being pretty good, though more opinion than scholarly. While not a noted historian the author is kinda a big deal.

Happy reading! :D
